page.layout: One page of running text. Above the text, the running head. Beside line 12 in the right margin, one marginal note ("Cap.7."). The underlining in brown ink is a manuscript annotation and is not printed.

main_text.l: tum,quos statim excitat. Quod proculdu-
bio haudquaquam præstaret, nisi spiritui,
qui cum minuitur, præsentaneum esset fo-
mentum,alimentumq;: At vinum, sicuti &
quatuor nostri corporis humores, ex qua-
tuor primis naturæ elementis constare nul-
limedico philosopho dubiũ est. Unde spi-
ritum ab ijsdem elementis suam primam
ducere originem,clarissimè patet: quādo-
quidem unũquodq; ex ijs alitur, è quibus
oritur.Posthac an uno spiritu duntaxat sit
præditū animal,scire licet. Fernelius enim
libro de Spiritu,& innato calido,præter cæ-
teros omnes medicos clariores diuidit spi-
ritus in quosdam innatos,quos stabiles, &
in unaquaque parte fixos esse ait, & in tres
alios errantes & vagos, qui per universum
corpus influit:unum videlicet naturalem
è iecore per venas in corporis extrema dif-
fusum:alterum vitalem, quem corasiduò [?]
per arterias in universum corpus emittit:
tertium animalem,qui in cerebri ventricu-
lis genitus,hincque per neruos profectus,
partes irrigat sensus motusque compotes.
In primis,quòd ad insitum spiritu attinet,
ipsum nō agnouerunt veteres medici, nec
certè ullum esse rationi consentaneum vi-
detur.

page.notes: Handwritten brown underlining over "an uno spiritu duntaxat sit præditū animal" and "libro de Spiritu" is manuscript, not print. Faint marks in the right margin are show-through or annotation and are left out. "corasiduò" is uncertain: the printed word may be "cor assiduò" in two words, so it is marked [?]. "quādo" is read from an acute-like mark over the a. The printed "dubiũ" and "unũquodq;" keep their tildes as printed.
